newsitem.title: USA: LL&E Louisiana well needs more testing.
newsitem.headline: LL&E Louisiana well needs more testing.

text.p: Louisiana Land and Exploration Co said Wednesday the C-1 well at South Fresh Water Bayou in Vermilion Parish in south Louisiana needs further testing to determine its commerciality.
The well was drilled to 21,000 feet and cased after hole logs had indicated potential hydrocarbon accumulations in the lower Miocene Discorbis 30 sand, the company said.
It has an 85 percent working interest in the well, while CMS Energy Corp owns 10 percent.
A number of intervals in the Discorbis 26 through 30 sands were perforated for testing, LL&E said.

While the upper portion of the Discorbis 30 was perforated and flowed 4.4 million cubic feet of gas and 472 barrels of condensate per day, perforations in the lower portion of the sand produced water. As a result of mechanical difficulties encountered during drilling and testing of this highly deviated, deep well and the reduced size of the potential hydrocarbon accumulation in this sand, the well was not completed in this interval, the company said.

In the Discorbis 26 sand, the well was perforated between 19,175 and 19,207 feet. During production tests, the zone flowed at rates up to 9.3 million cubic feet of natural gas and 333 barrels of condensate per day on a 14/64 inch choke with a flowing tubing pressure of 8,248 pounds per square inch, LL&E said.
It said testing of this sand will continue to determine the extent and commerciality of the zone.
